Ana (ML): Hello! Just accepted the org invite but `git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/llm-eval.git` fails with permission denied (publickey). I can see the repo in the web UI but cloning via SSH errors. Any hints?
Ravi (Platform): Hey @Ana, likely your SSH key isn't added to the GitHub account that has the org membership. Do `ssh -T git@github.com` and share output (don't paste the key). Also check https://github.com/settings/keys to confirm your key is present.
Ana (ML): `ssh -T` gives: "Permission denied (publickey)." I added my laptop key earlier today to my personal account, not sure if I added to the one that accepted the invite.
Kim (People Ops): We invited your work email (ana@redwood.ai). Could you confirm which GH username you used to accept? If it's your personal, we can re-send invite to the account with the key.
Ana (ML): I accepted on my personal username ana.dev. I want to use my work handle though (ana-redwood). I can move the key, but will that affect my personal repos?
Ravi (Platform): Best path: either add the same public key to the work account (safe) or use separate keys with an SSH config mapping host aliases to keys. For quick fix, paste your public key into https://github.com/settings/keys on the account that is a member of the org. After that, `ssh -T git@github.com` should say "Hi <username>! You've successfully authenticated".
Ana (ML): Added the key to ana-redwood and re-ran `ssh -T` — success: "Hi ana-redwood! You've successfully authenticated." Cloning now works. Thanks!
infra-bot: audit: ssh key added for user ana-redwood (id: ak-9876).
Ana (ML): Follow-up Q: should I delete the key from my personal account to avoid confusion?
Ravi (Platform): Not strictly necessary, but cleaner. If you keep the same key on both accounts it's fine. If you prefer separation, generate a work-specific key and update ~/.ssh/config. Kim, can People Ops note the common triage for SSH vs HTTPS onboarding?
Kim (People Ops): Yep will add a checklist item: "Add SSH key to GH account used for org invite or use separate keys with SSH config; verify with `ssh -T`". Thanks @Ravi.
Ana (ML): Great, closing this thread — appreciate the quick help. :tada:
